Task 01: 
Prompt inicial: 
You are an expert management consultant, organizational strategist and AI researcher. 
 
Context: 
The organization seeks to reduce operational complexity, improve energy efficiency, 
and deploy intelligent automation in a steelmaking/furnace scheduling environment. 
 
Your role is to analyze the provided document set as if you were preparing 
recommendations for senior executives. 
 
For every task: 
- Use only evidence from the uploaded documents. 
- Write in academic and professional English. 
- Avoid generic summaries. 
- Include critical analysis. 
- Use headings and subheadings. 
- Generate content suitable for direct export into Word and PDF. 
- Explicitly reference relationships between Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Digital 
Twins (DT), Explainable AI (XAI), Energy Efficiency, Furnace Scheduling and Industrial 
Automation whenever supported by the documents. 
I will provide tasks one at a time. 
 
Prompt 1: 
Task 1: Inventory and Initial Scan 
Analyze every uploaded document. 
For each document extract: 
- Title 
- Authors 
- Year 
- Journal / Conference 
- Keywords 
- Abstract Summary (100-150 words) 
- Main Contribution 
- Research Domain 

- Related Topics 
Then create: 
 
Section 1: Document Inventory Table 
 
Section 2: Knowledge Domain Boundary 
Identify: 
- Core themes 
- Secondary themes 
- Emerging themes 
- Technologies 
- Industrial applications 
 
 
Section 3: Initial Organizational Interpretation 
 
Explain how the collected documents contribute to solving: 
- Operational Complexity 
- Energy Efficiency 
- Intelligent Automation 
- Furnace Scheduling 
 
Finish with a one-page executive summary. 
Format the output as a professional report ready for PDF export. 
 
 
Report: 
Executive Summary: Strategic AI Architecture & Document Analysis for Steelmaking & 
Furnace Scheduling 
This executive report presents an analysis of 31 uploaded peer-reviewed research 
papers and technical benchmark studies. Designed for senior leadership, 
organizational strategists, and industrial AI researchers, this report analyzes the 
transformation of heavy metallurgical operations from rigid, energy-intensive shop 
floors into adaptive, energy-efficient, and transparent production ecosystems. 
Modern steel manufacturing operates under severe dynamic complexity driven by high 
variant diversity, fluctuating batch sizes, volatile spot electricity markets, stochastic 
equipment breakdowns, and thermal process constraints. Industrial furnace 
operations—such as Electric Arc Furnaces (EAFs), reheating furnaces, soaking pits, and 

heat treatment lines—represent the primary energy bottlenecks, accounting for up to 
70%–80% of direct thermal energy consumption. 
To resolve these operational hurdles, the literature establishes a four-pillar technology 
framework: 
1. Digital Twins (DT) & Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS): High-fidelity virtual replicas 
synchronized with physical plants via Industrial IoT, OPC-UA, Asset 
Administration Shells (AAS), and Service-Oriented Architectures (SOA) bridge 
traditional ERP/MES information silos to enable real-time tracking. 
2. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) & Multi-Agent Systems (MAS): Algorithms 
formulated under Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDP) and 
Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) optimize real-time 
production control, spot market energy purchasing, and multi-stage scheduling 
under uncertainty. 
3. Explainable AI (XAI) & Human-Centric Intelligence Augmentation (IA): Decision-
tree surrogates, SHAP feature attributions, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), 
and multi-objective counterfactual explanations convert "black-box" models 
into transparent, actionable insights, supporting human-in-the-loop (HiL) 
decision-making and operator fatigue management under Industry 5.0. 
4. Energy-Aware & Deterioration-Resilient Furnace Scheduling: Mathematical 
programming, matheuristics, and Pareto-based metaheuristics (NSGA-II, GWO, 
SAMOPSO) eliminate non-productive furnace idle times, manage slab 
deterioration, and balance by-product gas flows (BFG, COG, LDG). 
 
Exhaustive Analysis of Uploaded Literature 
Below is the structured extraction for all 31 documents in the knowledge base, 
categorized by metadata, abstract synthesis, primary contribution, research domain, 
and cross-cutting topics. 
 
Document 1: A polynomial-time scheduling approach to minimise idle energy 
consumption: An application to an industrial furnace 
• Title: A polynomial-time scheduling approach to minimise idle energy 
consumption: An application to an industrial furnace. 
• Authors: Ondřej Benedikt, Baran Alikoç, Přemysl Šůcha, Sergej Čelikovský, 
Zdeněk Hanzálek. 

• Year: 2021 (Available online 2020). 
• Journal / Conference: Computers & Operations Research, Vol. 128. 
• Keywords: Idle energy consumption, Single machine scheduling, Concave 
energy function, Shortest path problem, Industrial furnace, ŠKODA Auto case 
study. 
• Abstract Summary: Industrial heat-intensive processes like electric vacuum 
furnaces consume substantial power to maintain operating temperatures. This 
paper investigates single-machine scheduling with task release times, 
processing times, and deadlines to minimize idle energy consumption given a 
fixed task order. Proving that any concave idle energy consumption function 
allows transformation to a shortest path problem in a directed acyclic graph, the 
authors establish a polynomial-time algorithm with $O(n^3)$ computational 
complexity. Unlike Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) or time-indexed 
formulations, the complexity of this approach is independent of the scheduling 
horizon length. Tested on industrial data from ŠKODA Auto steel hardening lines, 
the approach yields optimal task start times and eliminates non-productive 
energy consumption efficiently. 
• Main Contribution: Proves that single-machine idle energy minimization under 
concave energy functions can be solved in $O(n^3)$ polynomial time 
independently of the scheduling horizon. 
• Research Domain: Operations Research & Industrial Energy Optimization. 
• Related Topics: Furnace Scheduling, Energy Efficiency, Mathematical 
Programming, Polynomial-Time Algorithms. 
 
Document 2: A proactive scheduling approach to steel rolling process with stochastic 
machine breakdown 
• Title: A proactive scheduling approach to steel rolling process with stochastic 
machine breakdown. 
• Authors: Lixin Tang, Yiyong Zhao, Jun Liu et al.. 
• Year: 2017. 
• Journal / Conference: Journal of Intelligent Manufacturing / Soft Computing. 
• Keywords: Proactive scheduling, Steel rolling, Stochastic machine breakdown, 
Support Vector Regression (SVR), NSGA-II, Soaking pit. 

• Abstract Summary: In ingot reheating and rolling processes, steel ingots are 
soaked in pits before transport to a rough mill. Stochastic disruptions such as 
machine breakdowns degrade schedule execution and increase resource 
consumption. This paper proposes a proactive scheduling framework using 
controllable processing time strategies to absorb breakdowns and preserve 
schedule stability. The authors integrate Support Vector Regression (SVR) to 
estimate schedule robustness and employ a surrogate-assisted Multi-Objective 
Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II) to optimize manufacturing costs, match-up times, 
and tardiness variance. Empirical validation on production data from a large 
Chinese steel enterprise demonstrates superior schedule stability and lower 
disruption recovery costs compared to traditional manual and deterministic 
rescheduling methods. 
• Main Contribution: Combines SVR machine learning with NSGA-II for proactive 
robust scheduling under stochastic breakdown, optimizing controllable 
processing times. 
• Research Domain: Stochastic Production Scheduling & Metallurgical 
Operations. 
• Related Topics: Steel Rolling, Ingot Soaking, Robust Optimization, Machine 
Breakdown. 
 
Document 3: A robust dynamic scheduling approach based on release time series 
forecasting for the steelmaking-continuous casting production 
• Title: A robust dynamic scheduling approach based on release time series 
forecasting for the steelmaking-continuous casting production. 
• Authors: Jianyu Long, Zhenzhong Sun, Panos M. Pardalos, Yun Bai, Shaohui 
Zhang, Chuan Li. 
• Year: 2020. 
• Journal / Conference: Applied Soft Computing Journal, Vol. 92. 
• Keywords: Steelmaking-continuous casting (SCC), Time series forecasting, 
Release time uncertainty, Robust dynamic scheduling, Multi-factor ANOVA. 
• Abstract Summary: Steelmaking-Continuous Casting (SCC) processes face 
dynamic operational perturbations caused by fluctuating charge release times 
from upstream refining stages. This paper formulates a robust dynamic 
scheduling approach driven by real-time release time series forecasting. By 
predicting future charge arrival windows, the scheduling algorithm proactively 

adjusts continuous caster allocations to minimize makespan and penalty costs. 
Multifactor Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and non-parametric Wilcoxon signed-
ranks statistical tests validate parameter configurations and performance 
improvements. Results confirm statistically significant reductions ($p < 0.05$) in 
total tardiness and wait-time disruptions over baseline evolutionary heuristics. 
• Main Contribution: Integrates time-series forecasting of job release dates into 
dynamic SCC scheduling, statistically proven via ANOVA and Wilcoxon tests. 
• Research Domain: Predictive Dynamic Scheduling & Soft Computing. 
• Related Topics: SCC Operations, Time Series Forecasting, Robustness, 
Evolutionary Computation. 
 
Document 4: Adapted techniques of explainable artificial intelligence for explaining 
genetic algorithms on the example of job scheduling 
• Title: Adapted techniques of explainable artificial intelligence for explaining 
genetic algorithms on the example of job scheduling. 
• Authors: Yu-Cheng Wang, Toly Chen. 
• Year: 2024 (Available online 2023). 
• Journal / Conference: Expert Systems With Applications, Vol. 237. 
• Keywords: Explainable AI (XAI), Genetic Algorithms (GA), Decision tree 
surrogate, Dynamic transition diagram, Job scheduling, Industry 4.0. 
• Abstract Summary: Genetic Algorithms (GAs) are widely applied to solve 
complex job shop scheduling problems, yet their metaheuristic mechanics 
(crossover, mutation, population selection) remain opaque "black boxes" to 
plant operators. This research adapts XAI techniques specifically for GA-based 
scheduling. The authors introduce decision-tree surrogate models to explain 
crossover and mutation operations, alongside novel Dynamic Transition and 
Contribution Diagrams using radar-scatter topologies to visualize chromosome 
evolution across iterations. Experimental evaluation confirms that these visual 
XAI tools significantly increase operator understandability, trust, and willingness 
to adopt automated scheduling outputs in manufacturing environments. 
• Main Contribution: Develops a comprehensive XAI toolkit (decision-tree 
surrogates and dynamic transition radar diagrams) to interpret GA search 
mechanics in manufacturing job scheduling. 

• Research Domain: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) & Manufacturing 
Decision Support. 
• Related Topics: Genetic Algorithms, Job Shop Scheduling, Human-AI Trust, 
Surrogates. 
 
Document 5: An Uncertainty Involved Two-Stage Energy Management Framework using 
Soft Actor-Critic 
• Title: An Uncertainty Involved Two-Stage Energy Management / Economic 
Dispatch Strategy for Steel Enterprises. 
• Authors: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics Authorship Group. 
• Year: 2025. 
• Journal / Conference: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics. 
• Keywords: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), By-product gas (BPG), Deep Reinforcement 
Learning (DRL), Two-stage economic dispatch, Energy fluctuation uncertainty. 
• Abstract Summary: Steel enterprise energy networks feature multi-media 
coupling across Coke Oven Gas (COG), Blast Furnace Gas (BFG), Linz-Donawitz 
Gas (LDG), steam, and power distribution grids. Due to severe demand and 
supply fluctuations, offline optimization models struggle with real-time 
dispatch. This paper proposes a Two-Stage Deep Soft Actor-Critic (2S-DSAC) 
DRL framework. Stage one uses mechanism-based mathematical models under 
diverse scenario samples to establish optimal baseline dispatch rules. Stage 
two trains a SAC policy network on these offline optimizations to execute instant 
online economic energy dispatch without repeatedly solving full mathematical 
programs. The system maintains strict consistency constraints across media 
connections while reducing operational energy costs under volatile load 
scenarios. 
• Main Contribution: Establishes a 2S-DSAC model combining mathematical 
mechanism baseline modeling with SAC reinforcement learning for rapid online 
by-product gas dispatch. 
• Research Domain: Industrial Energy Networks & Reinforcement Learning. 
• Related Topics: By-Product Gas, Soft Actor-Critic, Integrated Energy Systems, 
Real-Time Dispatch. 
 

Document 6: Assessing the Transparency and Explainability of AI Algorithms in Planning 
and Scheduling 
• Title: Assessing the Transparency and Explainability of AI Algorithms in Planning 
and Scheduling (The TUPLES Project). 
• Authors: Sara Morandini et al.. 
• Year: 2023. 
• Journal / Conference: European Commission Horizon Europe TUPLES Research 
Deliverable. 
• Keywords: Trustworthy AI, Explainable AI (XAI), Planning & Scheduling (P&S), Pre-
modeling, Interpretable models, Post-modeling, Actionability. 
• Abstract Summary: As part of the EU Horizon Europe TUPLES initiative, this work 
evaluates transparency and explainability frameworks for Planning and 
Scheduling (P&S) systems in manufacturing and logistics. The authors 
categorize XAI methods into pre-modeling (data debiasing), inherently 
interpretable models (decision trees, rule-based systems), and post-modeling 
techniques (LIME, SHAP, counterfactuals). The report emphasizes that in 
complex industrial scheduling, XAI must provide actionable, local, and global 
explanations to justify plan modifications, explain constraint unsatisfiability, and 
enable effective human-in-the-loop (HiL) supervision. Human-centered user 
interface flexibility and cognitive bias mitigation are identified as core 
imperatives for Trustworthy AI adoption. 
• Main Contribution: Formulates a structural taxonomy and human-centered 
design guidelines for operationalizing XAI in complex industrial planning and 
scheduling. 
• Research Domain: Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence & Operational Planning. 
• Related Topics: TUPLES Framework, Actionable Explanations, Human-in-the-
Loop, Counterfactuals. 
 
Document 7: Batch scheduling for minimal energy consumption and tardiness under 
uncertainties: A heat treatment application 
• Title: Batch scheduling for minimal energy consumption and tardiness under 
uncertainties: A heat treatment application. 
• Authors: Junkai Wang, Fei Qiao, Fu Zhao, John W. Sutherland. 

• Year: 2016. 
• Journal / Conference: CIRP Annals - Manufacturing Technology, Vol. 65. 
• Keywords: Energy efficiency, Batch scheduling, Heat treatment, Fuzzy logic, 
NSGA-II, Gas heating value uncertainty. 
• Abstract Summary: Heat treatment in steel production is an extreme thermal 
energy consumer, where pre-treatment ingot heating accounts for up to 70% of 
process energy (2–2.4 GJ/ton). Input parameters such as gas heating values, job 
processing times, and job arrival dates possess inherent real-world 
uncertainties. This paper formulates a multi-objective batch scheduling model 
for heat treatment furnaces to minimize total energy consumption and total 
weighted tardiness simultaneously. Triangular fuzzy numbers characterize 
parameter stochasticity, and fuzzy dominance logic is embedded into a Non-
dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Applied to a steel plant 
soaking operation, the fuzzy multi-objective optimization reveals high-quality 
Pareto-optimal trade-offs between delivery punctuality and gas consumption. 
• Main Contribution: Develops a fuzzy NSGA-II multi-objective batch scheduling 
model that accounts for uncertainties in gas caloric values and processing times 
in heat treatment furnaces. 
• Research Domain: Sustainable Manufacturing & Fuzzy Multi-Objective 
Scheduling. 
• Related Topics: Heat Treatment, Soaking Pits, Ingot Heating, Fuzzy Logic, Pareto 
Optimization. 
 
Document 8: Counterfactual Explanations in the Big Picture: An Approach for Job-Shop 
Scheduling Problems 
• Title: Counterfactual Explanations in the Big Picture: An Approach for Job-Shop 
Scheduling Problems. 
• Authors: ExPro Project Research Consortium / Cognitive Computation Authors. 
• Year: 2024. 
• Journal / Conference: Cognitive Computation, Vol. 16. 
• Keywords: Counterfactual explanations, Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP), 
Granular computing, Predictive process monitoring, NSGA-II, System-level 
recourse. 

• Abstract Summary: Standard counterfactual explanations in machine learning 
focus on local feature alterations without considering global systemic 
constraints. In Job-Shop Scheduling Problems (JSSP), modifying a single 
operation's resource allocation can cause ripple effects across total makespan 
and sequence feasibility. This paper proposes a multi-objective counterfactual 
optimization framework using Granular Computing and NSGA-II. Predictive 
process monitoring first estimates operation durations, followed by MILP 
schedule generation. NSGA-II then searches for actionable counterfactuals that 
balance operation feature proximity, execution duration reduction, overall 
makespan improvement, and schedule similarity. Evaluated on an industrial log 
of 161,109 operations across 31,628 jobs, the approach yields plausible, 
system-harmonious explanations for production planners. 
• Main Contribution: Introduces a granular computing multi-objective 
counterfactual explanation framework for JSSP that ensures local changes 
generate positive system-level scheduling outcomes. 
• Research Domain: Explainable AI (XAI) & Granular Process Optimization. 
• Related Topics: Counterfactuals, Granular Computing, Predictive Process 
Monitoring, JSSP, NSGA-II. 
 
Document 9: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Scheduling of a Steel Plant in the 
Electricity Spot Market 
• Title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Scheduling of a Steel Plant in the 
Electricity Spot Market. 
• Authors: Margi Shah, Yue Zhou, Jianzhong Wu, Max Mowbray. 
• Year: 2026 (Available online 2025). 
• Journal / Conference: Engineering (Elsevier / Chinese Academy of Engineering). 
• Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Industrial Demand Response 
(DR), Electricity spot market, POMDP, Electric Arc Furnace (EAF), Attention 
policy. 
• Abstract Summary: Steelmaking via Electric Arc Furnaces (EAF), Argon Oxygen 
Decarburization (AOD), and Ladle Furnaces (LF) is highly power-intensive, 
offering substantial load-shifting flexibility in real-time electricity spot markets. 
Scheduling under volatile day-ahead/spot prices and on-site Renewable Energy 
Source (RES) generation is modeled as a Partially Observable Markov Decision 
Process (POMDP) with state-specific action masking. The authors propose an 

attention-based DRL policy structure using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) 
combined with domain-knowledge heuristic priority rules (SPT, LPT, LEC, NDD). 
Experimental validation on Belgian Elia and Nord Pool spot market data 
demonstrates that the attention-DRL controller dynamically shifts heavy EAF 
melting loads to low-price periods, achieving lower energy costs while 
maintaining strict production deadline constraints. 
• Main Contribution: Develops a POMDP attention-based DRL scheduling agent 
with action-masking that optimizes steel plant EAF operations under electricity 
spot market volatility. 
• Research Domain: Industrial Demand Response & Deep Reinforcement 
Learning. 
• Related Topics: Spot Market Electricity, EAF Scheduling, POMDP, Attention 
Mechanism, Decarbonization. 
 
Document 10: Digital Twin and Scheduling of Parallel Walking Beam Reheating 
Furnaces 
• Title: Digital Twin and Scheduling of Parallel Walking Beam Reheating Furnaces. 
• Authors: Siyi Li, Ziyan Zhao, Shixin Liu, Yuying Jiang, Jianhai Song. 
• Year: 2026. 
• Journal / Conference: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics. 
• Keywords: Digital Twin (DT), Parallel machine scheduling, Walking beam 
reheating furnace, Steel manufacturing, Five-dimension DT. 
• Abstract Summary: Walking beam reheating furnaces heat steel slabs to 
specified rolling temperatures but present complex dynamic thermal and spatial 
constraints. This paper develops a closed-loop Five-Dimension Digital Twin (5D-
DT) architecture comprising physical entities, virtual entities, data space, 
services, and multi-protocol connections. The virtual entity incorporates a 
Three-Stage Model (TSM) executing operation representation, selection, and 
thermal-physical simulation. Real-time slab positions and furnace temperatures 
continuously synchronize the virtual model. When dynamic events occur (e.g., 
mill pauses, slab arrival changes), the DT service triggers adaptive re-
optimization heuristics to re-assign and re-sequence parallel walking furnaces. 
Physical validation confirms that closing the virtual-physical control loop 
significantly narrows the execution gap between algorithmic schedules and 
actual plant throughput. 

• Main Contribution: Formulates a 5D-DT framework with a Three-Stage Model for 
real-time parallel walking beam reheating furnace scheduling and state 
synchronization. 
• Research Domain: Cyber-Physical Systems & Intelligent Industrial Systems. 
• Related Topics: Digital Twins, Walking Beam Furnaces, Steel Reheating, Real-
Time Optimization. 
 
Document 11: Dynamic reallocation and rescheduling of steel products using agents 
with strategical anticipation and virtual market structures 
• Title: Dynamic reallocation and rescheduling of steel products using agents with 
strategical anticipation and virtual market structures. 
• Authors: Marcus J. Neuer, Francesca Marchiori, Alexander Ebel, Nikolaos 
Matskanis, Luca Piedimonti, Andreas Wolff, Gael Mathis. 
• Year: 2016. 
• Journal / Conference: IFAC-PapersOnLine, Vol. 49. 
• Keywords: Multi-agent systems (MAS), Service-oriented architecture (SOA), 
Semantic modeling, Off-spec products, Reallocation, Virtual market auctions. 
• Abstract Summary: In flat-steel hot rolling, process anomalies frequently 
produce off-spec coils that fail target quality specifications. Traditional 
hierarchical ERP/MES control structures lack cross-level communication to 
dynamically reallocate off-spec items. This research presents the I2MSteel 
holonic Multi-Agent System (MAS) built on Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) 
and Semantic MediaWiki ontologies. Product agents represent individual steel 
coils, using first-principle metallurgical models to anticipate future reachable 
states (e.g., alternative cold-rolling or galvanizing parameters). Order agents act 
as bidders in virtual market auctions. Deployed as an online open-loop 
prototype at an ArcelorMittal plant, the multi-agent market mechanism 
reallocates off-spec coils within milliseconds, reducing scrap and downgrade 
losses by ~25%. 
• Main Contribution: Implements an online holonic Multi-Agent virtual market 
system using semantic process modeling to dynamically reallocate off-spec 
steel products. 
• Research Domain: Distributed Multi-Agent Control & Industry 4.0 Systems. 

• Related Topics: Multi-Agent Systems, Off-Spec Reallocation, Hot Rolling, 
Service-Oriented Architecture, Semantic Ontologies. 
 
Document 12: Energy-Efficient Integration Optimization of Production Scheduling and 
Ladle Dispatching in Steelmaking Plants 
• Title: Energy-Efficient Integration Optimization of Production Scheduling and 
Ladle Dispatching in Steelmaking Plants. 
• Authors: Dayong Han, Qiuhua Tang, Zikai Zhang, Jun Cao. 
• Year: 2020. 
• Journal / Conference: IEEE Access, Vol. 8. 
• Keywords: Steelmaking-continuous casting (SCC), Ladle dispatching, Integrated 
optimization, Enhanced Migrating Birds Optimization (EMBO), Energy efficiency. 
• Abstract Summary: Steelmaking and Continuous Casting (SCC) represents an 
energy-intensive metallurgical phase where thermal loss during ladle 
transportation directly increases heating fuel overheads. Historically, 
production scheduling and ladle dispatching were decoupled. This paper 
formulates an integrated mathematical model with dual objectives: minimizing 
total weighted completion time (productivity) and total energy consumption. To 
solve this NP-hard problem, the authors develop an Enhanced Migrating Birds 
Optimization (EMBO) algorithm incorporating three-level heuristic solution 
generation, novel neighborhood search operators, simulated annealing 
acceptance criteria, and competitive mechanisms. Computational results 
confirm that integrated scheduling and ladle dispatching reduces total energy 
consumption by 1.21% while fully preserving plant productivity. 
• Main Contribution: Proposes an integrated optimization formulation and an 
Enhanced Migrating Birds Optimization (EMBO) algorithm for joint SCC 
scheduling and molten metal ladle dispatching. 
• Research Domain: Integrated Operations Research & Metallurgical Logistics. 
• Related Topics: Steelmaking-Continuous Casting, Ladle Dispatching, Migrating 
Birds Optimization, Energy Conservation. 
 
Document 13: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning For Production Control 
• Title: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning For Production Control. 

• Authors: Philipp Theumer, Florian Edenhofner, Roland Zimmermann, Alexander 
Zipfel. 
• Year: 2022. 
• Journal / Conference: 3rd Conference on Production Systems and Logistics 
(CPSL 2022). 
• Keywords: Production control, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Multi-Agent 
Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Explainable AI (XAI), SHAP values. 
• Abstract Summary: Rising product customization increases dynamic complexity 
in job-shop production, overwhelming human operators during unexpected 
disruptions. While Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Multi-Agent 
Reinforcement Learning (MARL) achieve high decision quality and rapid 
response times, their "black-box" nature prevents operator trust. This study 
integrates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values into a PPO-trained 
MARL production control system. SHAP post-hoc attribution localizes feature 
contributions (e.g., buffer levels, machine queue states, job priorities) for every 
control action. Benchmarked against standard industrial rule-based controllers 
(RBCs), the explainable MARL framework yields superior scheduling 
performance while displaying visual explanations that establish human 
supervisory trust. 
• Main Contribution: Combines MARL production control with SHAP feature 
attribution to provide transparent, explainable real-time order dispatching 
decisions. 
• Research Domain: Explainable Reinforcement Learning & Industrial Control 
Systems. 
• Related Topics: Production Control, MARL, XAI, SHAP, Rule-Based Control, 
Dynamic Complexity. 
 
Document 14: GA-BP prediction model for energy consumption of reheating furnace in 
hot rolling steel production 
• Title: GA-BP prediction model for energy consumption of reheating furnace in 
hot rolling steel production. 
• Authors: Yi Duan, Guang Chen, Xiangjun Bao, Jing Xu, Lu Zhang, Xiaojing Yang. 
• Year: 2025. 
• Journal / Conference: Scientific Reports (Nature Publisher). 

• Keywords: Reheating furnace, Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), 
Genetic Algorithm (GA), Energy consumption prediction, Gas consumption, Hot 
rolling. 
• Abstract Summary: Reheating furnaces in hot rolling mills consume massive 
quantities of fossil fuels, making accurate energy consumption prediction vital 
for operational optimization. Traditional Backpropagation (BP) neural networks 
frequently suffer from slow convergence and local minima stagnation. This study 
constructs a hybrid Genetic Algorithm-Backpropagation (GA-BP) predictive 
model. The Genetic Algorithm globally optimizes the initial weight and bias 
distribution of the BP network prior to gradient training. Trained on multi-factor 
industrial datasets (billet dimensions, steel grades, residence times, zone 
temperatures), the GA-BP model exhibits superior predictive accuracy, lower 
Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and robust regression fit compared to standard BP 
and PSO-BP baselines, enabling real-time energy evaluation and firing 
adjustments. 
• Main Contribution: Develops a hybrid GA-BP neural network model for accurate 
multi-factor prediction of reheating furnace gas consumption in hot rolling lines. 
• Research Domain: Industrial Energy Modeling & Computational Intelligence. 
• Related Topics: Reheating Furnaces, Energy Prediction, Genetic Algorithms, BP 
Neural Networks, Hot Rolling. 
 
Document 15: Heating furnace scheduling with grey wolf optimization 
• Title: Heating furnace scheduling with grey wolf optimization. 
• Authors: Chen Rao, Jianxin Zhang. 
• Year: 2025. 
• Journal / Conference: Journal of Physics: Conference Series, Vol. 2993. 
• Keywords: Heating furnace scheduling, Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Hot strip 
rolling, Energy optimization, Slab heating pattern. 
• Abstract Summary: Reheating furnace scheduling directly influences energy 
efficiency and rolling continuity in hot strip mills. Furnace loading schedules 
must account for mixed slab charging, machine unavailability constraints, and 
temperature transition penalties. This paper applies a Grey Wolf Optimizer 
(GWO) metaheuristic to optimize slab charging sequences and heating 
durations. Modulating wolf leadership hierarchical mechanisms ($\alpha, \beta, 

\delta$), the GWO balances global exploration and local refinement to minimize 
energy consumption and slab delay costs. Comparison against standard genetic 
and differential evolution algorithms shows that GWO achieves faster 
convergence and superior objective values in multi-furnace industrial instances. 
• Main Contribution: Formulates a Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) scheme tailored 
for parallel heating furnace charging and sequence optimization. 
• Research Domain: Swarm Intelligence & Metallurgical Scheduling. 
• Related Topics: Heating Furnaces, Grey Wolf Optimizer, Hot Rolling, Energy 
Efficiency. 
 
Document 16: Human-Centric Job-Shop Production Planning and Scheduling System 
Based on the Concept of Industry 5.0 
• Title: Human-Centric Job-Shop Production Planning and Scheduling System 
Based on the Concept of Industry 5.0. 
• Authors: Waqas Javaid, Saif Ullah. 
• Year: 2026. 
• Journal / Conference: Journal of Engineering (John Wiley & Sons). 
• Keywords: Industry 5.0 (I5.0), Digital Twin (DT), Dynamic Break Integration (DBI), 
Human-Centricity, Smartwatches, Operator fatigue. 
• Abstract Summary: While Industry 4.0 emphasizes fully autonomous 
automation, it frequently ignores operator fatigue and human cognitive 
concentration, degrading schedule execution robustness. Aligning with Industry 
5.0 principles, this research develops a Digital Twin (DT) Production Planning 
and Scheduling system incorporating Dynamic Break Integration (DBI). 
Operators wear smartwatches that transmit real-time telemetry on microbreaks, 
fatigue status, and situational feedback to the DT. When fatigue or unplanned 
microbreaks occur, the DT performs local adaptive replanning. Industrial job-
shop testing demonstrated a 42.6% reduction in downtime, an 8.8% decrease in 
cycle time, a 12.3% increase in actual working time, and a 23.9% overall 
productivity gain, proving the value of human-centric cyber-physical 
collaboration. 
• Main Contribution: Implements an Industry 5.0 smartwatch-connected Digital 
Twin PPS system with Dynamic Break Integration for real-time fatigue 
management and human-centric rescheduling. 

• Research Domain: Industry 5.0 & Human-Centric Cyber-Physical Systems. 
• Related Topics: Digital Twins, Dynamic Break Integration, Operator Fatigue, 
Human-Machine Collaboration, Smartwatches. 
 
Document 17: Integrated Multi-Objective Optimization for Reheating Furnace 
Scheduling and Hot Rolling Plan 
• Title: Integrated Multi-Objective Optimization for Reheating Furnace Scheduling 
and Hot Rolling Plan. 
• Authors: Shujin Jia, Weigang Lin, Bin Du et al.. 
• Year: 2022. 
• Journal / Conference: Proceedings of the 34th Chinese Control and Decision 
Conference (CCDC 2022). 
• Keywords: Reheating furnace allocation, Hot rolling scheduling, Multi-objective 
optimization, Slab jumping penalty, Ant colony optimization. 
• Abstract Summary: Hot rolling consumes over 10% of total steel mill energy, 
with reheating furnaces constituting the primary thermal process unit. Reheating 
furnace allocation and hot rolling sequencing are interdependent: mismatched 
furnace discharging creates rolling delays, while improper rolling sequences 
cause excessive width/thickness jumping penalties. This paper establishes an 
integrated multi-objective optimization model. The objective function minimizes 
adjacent slab jumping penalties (width, thickness, hardness) while maximizing 
rolling unit capacity and minimizing furnace heating residence times. Solved via 
a multi-objective ant colony algorithm, the integrated approach outperforms 
sequential two-stage planning by harmonizing furnace delivery paces with mill 
rolling constraints. 
• Main Contribution: Develops an integrated multi-objective mathematical 
optimization model connecting reheating furnace allocation directly with hot 
rolling sequence generation. 
• Research Domain: Integrated Systems Optimization & Hot Rolling Logistics. 
• Related Topics: Reheating Furnaces, Hot Rolling Plans, Jumping Penalties, Ant 
Colony Algorithm. 
 
Document 18: Intelligent optimization method for the dynamic scheduling of hot metal 
ladles of one-ladle technology on ironmaking and steelmaking interface in steel plants 

• Title: Intelligent optimization method for the dynamic scheduling of hot metal
